models_evaluated: two unnamed deep learning models predicting biomarkers from whole slide images

links.outcome: Deep learning biomarker prediction versus simple pathologist-assigned grade baseline
links.effect: Because of biomarker correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages over pathologist-assigned grades for predicting certain biomarkers. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
links.quote: We also show that, due to the presence of such correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages in predicting certain biomarkers in comparison to simply using pathologist-assigned grades for their prediction.

unlisted_practices: Test biomarker predictors for confounding by co-dependent biomarkers using permutation testing and stratification analysis
Define prediction variables or group patients by biomarker co-dependencies during model development

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates confounding and shortcut learning in deep learning computational pathology models predicting omics biomarkers, highlighting critical methodological and bias issues but not testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
